newsitem.title: UK: British octuplets buried in same grave.
newsitem.headline: British octuplets buried in same grave.

text.p: Eight octuplets, stillborn to a woman whose rare pregnancy raised controversy in Britain over fertility treatment and tabloid journalism, were laid to rest in a single grave on Monday.
Mother Mandy Allwood clung to her partner Paul Hudson in tears as the eight babies, each in a white wooden coffin, were lowered into the ground at West Norwood cemetery, southeast London.

The six boys and two girls -- Kypros, Donald, Adam, Nelson, Cassius, Martyn, Kitali and Layne -- weighed about 200 grams (seven ounces) each and were small enough for each to be held in the palm of one hand.
The couple had written messages to each of the babies on cards laid on the wreaths next to the grave.
One read: "To Cassius, the last to die. You gave us hope right to the very end, but we know this is just the beginning. Yours always, Mum and Dad".
The eight were stillborn less than two weeks ago over three days in the 19th week of Allwood's pregnancy, at King's College hospital in London.

The congregation was small, consisting mainly of family and friends. Also present were Allwood's publicist Max Clifford and two reporters from Britain's best selling tabloid newspaper the News of the World, to whom she sold her story.
